cells.tense: The whole thing is here now, and you are at the desk with the pen.
cells.ask: Tell one person exactly what they gave to this, specific enough that they could repeat it back. Hand over the piece of the picture that has their name on it.
cells.core:
Here is what is going well. You can feel the whole span of something — start, middle, the effort people gave — and you can still hold your direction while you feel it. Most people manage one or the other. You keep both, so the people walking with you know they are part of it, and you do not have to choose between getting there and being with them.

You feel the room and you feel the road at the same time. Notice one thing about this that is worth keeping: when it is running, it does not feel like managing anything. A quiet breakfast with someone who was in it with you, no work talk — that is what keeps the two sides of this in one room. Keep them there.
cells.sheetLine: You feel the whole picture and keep moving, and both stay open.
cells.verb: knowing the whole picture and letting it be complete enough to move on
cells.place: in the part of life that keeps steady direction toward a goal

cells.tense: You are already standing at the end, rehearsing how it will land before it has happened.
cells.ask: Before one more move on this, say out loud what is actually finished today. Then stop for the day.
cells.core:
You are running finished before it is finished. The ending gets decided in advance — who will have felt what, when you will know it worked, what the last step will be — and every step now has to serve that ending. The push you are putting into it is real, but it is aimed at a moment that has not arrived.

The strange part is that the recognition you are working toward is already happening, quietly, and you keep skipping over it to get to the version where it is certain. Reactive push, a decision made at speed to close the gap, is not the same as closure. A real ending still does not have to tell you it is one.
cells.sheetLine: You are writing the ending before the middle has happened.

cells.tense: You were somewhere the feeling did not land well, and you have been holding there since.
cells.ask: Say one sentence about how today is going to someone this week, and let it be small — no setup, no follow-up question needed.
cells.core:
You are not arriving where you are going, and the direction is not the problem. The spark has gone quiet. Nothing has felt new in a while, so nothing gets started fresh, and then the days feel the same, which makes it harder to start anything at all.

You know how to walk toward something. The feeling of being inside it while you do, that part is thin right now, and you have been treating the thinness as proof that the goal is not worth it. It does not mean that. A beginning is supposed to feel a little small and a little unfinished.
cells.sheetLine: Direction is there, the spark has gone quiet.

cells.tense: You are steering this with a clear sense of what is fair and still calling it circumstance.
cells.ask: Pick one choice you are already making about this and say 'I chose that' — out loud, once, no audience needed.
cells.core:
You already run a fair accounting inside this. You can tell where the effort belongs, who is owed what, when to give and when to hold back, and it moves through you faster than thinking does. Then you describe it as the situation — the schedule, what they needed, the way it worked out.

That knowing is the thing steering your momentum, not a feeling riding along behind it. You are not calculating more than other people. You are just the one making the calls, and you have been reading the calls as something that happened to you. Some of the fairness has felt one-sided, and a fair accounting is one you would notice being inside of.
